title: Great American Family Selects CTS For Channel Origination, Playout, Transmission
body_html:
What Was Announced

Great American Family has selected CTS for its channel origination, playout, and transmission needs, marking a significant decision in the broadcaster's technical operations. This move involves outsourcing critical components of its broadcast workflow to a third-party provider, which can have implications for the broadcaster's operational efficiency, cost structure, and editorial control. The announcement highlights the growing trend of broadcasters seeking specialized vendors to manage specific aspects of their operations, allowing them to focus on core competencies such as content creation and programming.

The Engineering and Operational Significance

The decision by Great American Family to outsource its channel origination, playout, and transmission to CTS is technically significant because it involves the integration of new systems and workflows into the broadcaster's existing infrastructure. From an engineering perspective, this move may enable the broadcaster to simplify its operations, reduce costs, and improve reliability by leveraging CTS's expertise and resources. The use of a third-party provider can also facilitate the adoption of new technologies and standards, such as IP-based playout and SMPTE ST 2110, which can provide greater flexibility and scalability in broadcast operations. Furthermore, the outsourcing of playout and transmission can allow Great American Family to focus on the creative aspects of its business, while relying on CTS to manage the technical complexities of getting its channels to air.

Industry Context

The move by Great American Family to outsource its channel origination, playout, and transmission is consistent with the broader trend of broadcasters seeking to increase their operational efficiency and reduce costs through the use of specialized vendors and cloud-based services. This approach is often referred to as a "hybrid" or "virtualized" playout model, where certain components of the broadcast workflow are managed by a third-party provider, while others remain in-house. Comparable approaches can be seen in the use of cloud-based media asset management (MAM) systems, which allow broadcasters to manage their content libraries and automate workflows without having to maintain complex on-premise infrastructure. The decision by Great American Family to partner with CTS also reflects the growing importance of interoperability and standards-based interfaces, such as AES67 and SMPTE ST 2110, which enable the seamless integration of different systems and vendors in the broadcast chain.

Implications for Broadcast and Media Teams

The decision by Great American Family to outsource its channel origination, playout, and transmission has significant implications for broadcast and media teams, particularly in terms of the skills and expertise required to manage these operations. As broadcasters increasingly rely on third-party vendors and cloud-based services, there is a growing need for engineers and operations managers to have a deep understanding of the technical and business implications of these decisions. This includes the ability to evaluate the performance and reliability of outsourced services, manage complex workflows and integrations, and ensure that the broadcaster's overall operations remain resilient and secure. Furthermore, the use of specialized vendors and cloud-based services requires broadcast and media teams to be highly adaptable and agile, with the ability to respond quickly to changes in the market, technology, and viewer behavior. By carefully evaluating the technical and operational implications of outsourcing critical components of their workflow, broadcasters can ensure that they are well-positioned to thrive in a rapidly changing media landscape.
